# BLAKE2 F test vectors

## Official BLAKE2b vectors

`blake2b-kat.txt` is copied verbatim from the official BLAKE2 repository:

- Source: https://github.com/BLAKE2/BLAKE2/blob/ed1974ea83433eba7b2d95c5dcd9ac33cb847913/testvectors/blake2b-kat.txt
- Revision: `ed1974ea83433eba7b2d95c5dcd9ac33cb847913`
- Git blob: `d9438ef101bf69249514731671257c0ef3009db9`

The 256 known-answer vectors use BLAKE2b-512 with a 64-byte key and messages
of lengths 0 through 255 bytes. The unit test next to `compress` assembles
keyed BLAKE2b hashes using the compression function under test, then compares
each complete digest with the official expected hash. This exercises 12 rounds,
key-block processing, final and non-final blocks, and message-block boundaries.
The hash framing exists only in the test module. Expected hashes are not generated
by our implementation. Tests need no external tools or network access.

```sh
cargo test -p airbender-crypto --lib blake2f_matches_official_blake2b_vectors
```

To refresh the fixture, copy `testvectors/blake2b-kat.txt` from a reviewed upstream
revision and update the revision and blob above. `git hash-object` verifies that
the checked-in file matches the pinned upstream blob.

## EIP-152 vectors

The BLAKE2b vectors only run 12 rounds and never set the high counter word `t1`,
so they don't catch a wrong message schedule after round 12 or a dropped `t1`.
`eip152-vectors.txt` covers both. Each record is a `name`, an input in the 213-byte
EIP-152 precompile encoding (rounds as a big-endian `u32`, then `h`, `m`, `t` and
the final-block flag), and the expected 64-byte output. The name says where the
vector comes from, and none of the expected outputs is generated by our
implementation.

`eip152-vector-4` to `eip152-vector-7` are test vectors 4 to 7 of EIP-152, copied
verbatim (rounds 0, 12 with and without the final flag, and 1). Vectors 0 to 3 are
malformed inputs that the precompile rejects, and `compress` can't express them
(its arguments are fixed-size and the flag is a `bool`). They are left out, and so
is vector 8, which runs `0xffffffff` rounds and is too slow for a unit test.

- Source: https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/blob/5510973b40973b6aa774f04c9caba823c8ff8460/EIPS/eip-152.md#test-cases
- Git blob: `2762bfcff3e549ef263342e5239ef03ac2b07400`

The `eest-` vectors come from the Ethereum execution spec tests and are named by
their `id`. They are the successful cases of `test_blake2b` (rounds 12 to 1024,
with `t0` set to 3, 5, 16 or 120) except the four that repeat EIP-152 vectors 4
to 7, plus the 100,000-round case of `test_blake2b_large_gas_limit`. The suite's
8,000,000-round case is left out to keep the test fast. Inputs are encoded the way
the suite's `Blake2bInput.create_blake2b_tx_data` encodes them, with the defaults
from `common.py` and `spec.py`. The output is `data_1` followed by `data_2`, each
left-padded to 32 bytes, because the suite writes some of them without leading
zeros.

- Source: https://github.com/ethereum/execution-spec-tests/tree/ca37419a162757c644c61829331321e36243547b/tests/istanbul/eip152_blake2
- Git blobs: `test_blake2.py` `2f600a1fd9e7150434059d282d7544ff6dd83dbe`, `common.py` `06f499308339497f7d6c338143ab2239370da56c`, `spec.py` `021c94a28d0177fa13667558e24090de72156c3a`

None of these sources has a vector with a nonzero `t1`, and neither do geth's
precompile vectors, its `blake2b_f_test.go` or RFC 7693 appendix A. So
`computed-rounds-20-high-counter` is computed. It runs 20 rounds on the `h` and `m`
of the EIP-152 vectors, with `t` set to the bytes `00` to `0f` (so
`t0 = 0x0706050403020100` and `t1 = 0x0f0e0d0c0b0a0908`) and the final flag set.
Its expected output comes from two independent implementations that agree: geth's
generic Go F (`crypto/blake2b/blake2b_generic.go` at
`cbf0b5bc92c4ba857d79778f646f0b6b9507d07f`, git blob
`4d3f69d292d00312d42b3b3e5d9a9090896e443e`), and a Python F written from RFC 7693
that matches `hashlib.blake2b`. Neither is checked in. Both also reproduce every
published vector in the file.

```sh
cargo test -p airbender-crypto --lib blake2f_matches_eip152_vectors
```
